title: Towards Predictability of Dominant Cognitive Biases: Intersection of Cultural, Generational and Psychological Models
abstract: Cognitive biases are evolutionarily adaptive mental shortcuts rooted in automatic processing, yet their expression varies widely across individuals due to differences in personality structure, cultural communication patterns, and generational socialization. Drawing on research in behavioural psychology, cognitive science, organizational behaviour, and cross-cultural communication, this paper presents an integrated exploratory framework for identifying probabilistic dominant cognitive bias profiles by combining three complementary models: Kahler's process communication model, Lewis's cultural communication model, and Strauss and Howe' generational cohort theory. The study outlines the design of an 11-item instrument grounded in these frameworks and evaluates its preliminary validity, reliability and perceived accuracy. Unlike single-dimensional psychometric tests, the suggested model combines psychological, cultural, and temporal factors to suggest how these elements interact to shape bias tendencies. It offers insight into how dominant biases serve as sensemaking filters through which individuals interpret organizational purpose, challenge assumptions, and adapt their decision-making in uncertain environments. This predictive approach also supports talent mapping, and the formation of cognitively diverse teams, which strengthen strategic adaptability, and contribute to more effective and inclusive organizational practices.

title: Organizational Purpose in Crisis Contexts: Executive Sensemaking and Adaptive Governance
abstract: This study examines how organizational purpose is constructed and enacted in crisis contexts, addressing the limitations of static and declarative approaches to purpose in existing literature. It seeks to explain how executives mobilize purpose when organizations face uncertainty, moral ambiguity, and competing stakeholder demands, and why a processual understanding of purpose is necessary in volatile environments. The article adopts a qualitative, theory-building research design based on 15 semi-structured interviews with senior executives and governance actors operating in crisis-exposed organizations. The findings show that organizational purpose functions as a dynamic sensemaking and governance resource rather than a fixed reference point. Purpose anchors executive interpretation under uncertainty, frames ethical trade-offs, mediates stakeholder pluralism, and legitimizes adaptive governance responses during crises. This study advances understanding of purpose as ethical navigation in contexts of moral pluralism and offers a framework for analyzing purpose enactment in crisis governance, with implications for future research and leadership practice.

title: Purpose in Innovation, Strategy and Organizational Transformation
abstract: Corporate purpose is the foundation for an organization’s existence. The concept has evolved from shareholder profit to a strategic driver, merging profit to environmental and societal needs. Despite its revival, literature remains disjointed regarding how purpose restores organizational transformation. This paper offers a conceptual model of how corporate purpose acts as a strategic asset in strategic renewal, digital transformation and innovation ecosystems, legitimising change and enhancing resilience, while helping to guide organizations in an ethical manner including in the responsible adoption of technologies such as AI. Purpose also functions as an "alarm system" in highly competitive markets while conquering business myopia, in order to stimulate innovation ecosystems. Additionally, the challenges of a purpose-led transformation are identified along with a multi-layered diagram depicting how a corporate purpose catalyses these three enabling properties (credibility, context-sensitivity, conversability), while strengthening adaptability and legitimacy. Significantly, the model emphasises cross-institutional differences, improving governance in emerging markets with weaker regulatory systems, while it reinforces legitimacy and compliance in developed economies.

title: Ethical Governance of AI and Organizational Resilience in Healthcare: Reframing Organizational Purpose Under Multipolar Crisis Conditions
abstract: This article demonstrates that managerial AI systems play a constitutive role in redefining organizational purpose during crisis. Rather than merely supporting decision-making, AI systems function as sensemaking infrastructures that shape executive interpretations of organizational performance, risk, and stakeholder priorities. Drawing on an integrative review of literature on organizational purpose, AI ethics, healthcare management, and crisis governance, alongside an analysis of European and French regulatory frameworks, the study conceptualizes AI as an ethical and political mediator of stakeholder conflict. The analysis identifies a set of interrelated ethical dynamics: purpose drift toward short-term operational stability, selective visibility of stakeholder claims, normalization of algorithmic arbitration in morally plural contexts, and fragmentation of accountability in crisis governance. This paper draws up a conceptual framework that positions ethical AI governance as a core component of organizational resilience.

title: Operationalizing Corporate Purpose Through ESG: A TPB Analysis of Consumer Cognition and Purchase Behaviour

author.name: Onewo Theophilus Tobi Eshiozemoghie, Zhanna Sergeevna Belyaeva

abstract: This paper examines how the theory of planned behaviour (TPB) influence ESG purchases, offering insights into how articulated purpose is validated through consumer markets. The results from the structural equation modelling and surveying 362 Unilever Nigeria customers, show that attitude toward ESG products is the strongest driver of purchase intentions, followed by perceived behavioural control and subjective norms. The study further analyzes the moderating effect of demographic factors on the relationship between these psychosocial determinants and ESG purchasing. By integrating TPB with ESG, this research explains how corporate purpose transitions from statement to stakeholder experience and offers actionable insights for leaders seeking to align corporate purpose with authentic market engagement, thereby enhancing both societal impact and commercial relevance in an era defined by digital transformation and heightened socio-ecological expectations.
